battle.name: 陳慶之攻北魏之戰
battle.brief: 529年四月，梁將陳慶之護北魏北海王元顥北還，攻克滎城，進至睢陽。魏將丘大千率眾七萬分築九城拒守，陳慶之一日連下三城，逼其投降；再拔考城，俘征東將軍元暉業，直趨大梁，魏軍望風而降。卡面羅馬弩砲代表的重砲攻城技術，正是這場攻城戰的通用手段。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 這場戰爭是529年南梁對北魏的一場大規模北伐，交戰主體是兩個正在從內部失序的南北王朝。梁方以梁武帝蕭衍為最高決策者，行動由他直接授權：528年十月，他接納北魏北海王元顥，以之為魏王，派東宮直閣將軍陳慶之率兵七千人護送元顥北還。梁軍的骨幹是陳慶之自行招集的精騎與輕裝步卒，裝甲從簡、以速度取勝；沿途各州鎮提供的兵員、糧秣與水陸轉運由後方接應，而這條補給線在深入之後迅速拉長到極限。北伐軍的指揮鏈極短：帝命直達將帥，陳慶之自假節、飈勇將軍而至使持節、鎮北將軍、護軍、前軍大都督，權柄隨戰果而升，幾乎一人獨斷。魏方的局面則是皇權與權臣互相絞纏：孝莊帝元子攸在位，而兵權與北方邊鎮的調動權握在晉陽大將爾朱榮手中，州郡守將各守其境，不相統一。睢陽一線的守軍是徐州方面的丘大千，眾七萬、分築九城；考城是征東將軍濟陰王元暉業所部羽林庶子二萬；滎陽由左僕射楊昱、西河王元悰、撫軍將軍元顯恭率御仗、羽林、宗子、庶子共約七萬據守；虎牢則由爾朱世隆與西荊州刺史王羆率騎一萬扼守。援軍的成分更能說明北魏的結構：上黨王元天穆以大將軍身分統軍南下，驃騎將軍爾朱吐沒兒領胡騎五千，騎將魯安領夏州步騎九千，另有王老生、費穆二萬據虎牢，刁宣、刁雙分入梁、宋兩地。梁軍推進之所以如入無境，正是因為魏方同時在北面應付幽州邢杲起義、在南面分兵、又在晉陽集結大軍，兵力被拉成數條互不相救的線。
countriesEn: This war was a large-scale northern expedition by the Southern Liang against Northern Wei in 529, fought between two dynasties that were each coming apart from within. On the Liang side Liang Wudi Emperor Xiaoyan was the ultimate decision-maker, and the operation was authorised by him directly: in October 528 he took in the Northern Wei Prince of Beihai Yuan Hong, made him King of Wei, and sent the Eastern Palace direct pavilion general Chen Qingzhi with seven thousand men to escort Yuan Hong back north. The backbone of the Liang army was the cavalry and light infantry Chen Qingzhi had gathered himself, lightly equipped and winning on speed; the troops, grain and river-and-road transport supplied by the departments along the route came from the rear, and that line of supply stretched to its limit once the column went deep. The chain of command on the Liang side was very short: the emperor's orders went straight to the general, and Chen Qingzhi's authority grew with his successes, from acting commissioner and general of rushing courage to imperial commissioner, general who pacifies the north, protector, and chief commander of the vanguard, so that in practice one man decided. The Wei side was a case of throne and strongman twisting each other: Emperor Xiaozhuang Yuan Ziyou sat on the throne while the power of decision over the northern garrisons sat with Erzhu Rong, the commander at Jinyang, and the regional governors each held his own ground without any common plan. On the Suiyang line the defenders were Qiu Daqian of the Xu region, seventy thousand men distributed in nine forts; at Kaocheng stood Yuan Huiye, general who conquers the east and Prince of Jiyin, with twenty thousand of the imperial Feathered Guard; at Xingyang the left director of the ministries Yang Yu, Prince of Xiyuan Yuan Jiong and general of pacification Yuan Xiangong held some seventy thousand of the imperial guard, the Feathered Guard, the sons of the imperial clan and the sons of noble families; and at Hulao, Erzhu Shilong with the inspector of Western Jing, Wang Ji, held ten thousand cavalry. The composition of the relief armies says more about the structure of Northern Wei: the Prince of Shangdang Yuan Tianmu came south as general-in-chief, the general of the agile cavalry Erzhu Tumo'er brought five thousand Hu horsemen, the cavalry commander Lu An brought nine thousand foot and horse of the Xia prefecture, and Wang Laosheng and Fei Mu held two more at Hulao while Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang entered Liang and Song. The Liang advance met almost no resistance only because Wei was stretched at once: tied down in the north by the rising of Xing Gao, split to the south, and meanwhile massing a great army at Jinyang, its strength was pulled into several lines that could not support one another.
people: 陳慶之（484至539年），字子雲，義興郡國山縣（今江蘇宜興）人，是這場北伐的靈魂。他幼年隨梁武帝起兵，東下平建鄴後做過主書，散盡家財招集將士，等的只是一個機會；528年十月受命護元顥北還時，他手中的兵只有七千。史載他性格謹慎，每奉詔必洗沐拜受；生活儉樸，只穿素衣，不好絲竹；射不穿札、不善騎馬，卻善撫軍士，能得其死力——這幾句描寫說明他的本事不在個人技藝，而在士氣與組織。梁武帝在渦陽之戰後賜他的手詔寫道：本非將種，又非豪家，觖望風雲，以至於此，可深思奇略，善克令終，開朱門而待賓，揚聲名於竹帛，豈非大丈夫哉。梁方另一個關鍵人物是被北伐的元顥：他是北魏宗室、北海王，趁北魏內亂投奔南梁，取得魏王之號，於睢陽城南稱帝，進而攻大梁、入滎陽、據洛陽宮，改元大赦，一度又想擺脫梁廷自立，因此始終是梁軍的助力也是累贅，最終在河橋兵敗被擒，押至臨潁遇害。魏方最關鍵的人物是爾朱榮：他是晉陽的實際統帥，能在數月之內把北方邊鎮的兵馬抽調南下，也能用木筏夜渡黃河破掉對手的河防；孝莊帝元子攸在這場戰爭中從皇帝淪為他手中的棋子，退保長子、奔往並州。地方將領中，丘大千以九城拒睢陽而一日失三城，被迫投降；元暉業在考城被俘；滎陽的楊昱等苦守，魯安在陣前倒戈；攻滎陽時，東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣兩名壯士率先登城。撤軍途中，豫州人程道雍等人暗中護送陳慶之出汝陰返建康，使他免於被擒。
peopleEn: Chen Qingzhi, born 484 and died in 539, courtesy name Ziyun, a native of Guoshan county in Yixing commandery, in what is now Yixing in Jiangsu, was the soul of this northern expedition. He followed Liang Wudi from childhood, served as a secretary of the prince's writing office after the march east to capture Jiankang, scattered his own money to gather soldiers and officers, and was only waiting for an opportunity; when he was ordered in October 528 to escort Yuan Hong north he had seven thousand men under his hand. The histories describe him as careful and reverent, washing and bowing to receive every imperial command; simple in his living, wearing plain white garments and disliking music and singing; unable to shoot an arrow through a lamellar plate and not a horseman, yet skilled at managing his soldiers and able to win their willingness to die for him. Those few lines show that his gift lay not in personal skill but in morale and organisation. After the battle of Woyang, Liang Wudi sent him a handwritten edict saying: you were not born of a line of generals nor of a great house, yet you longed for the moment of fortune until it came; study deeply your uncommon strategy and carry it well to the end; open the red gate to welcome guests, spread your fame through the bamboo and silk, is this not what a great man should be? The other key figure on the Liang side was the man being escorted, Yuan Hong: a member of the Northern Wei imperial clan, Prince of Beihai, who fled to the south amid the disorder of the north, obtained the title of King of Wei, proclaimed himself emperor south of the city of Suiyang, pressed on to take Daliang, took Xingyang and entered the Luoyang palace, changed the era and issued a general pardon, and at one point meant to break free of the Liang court and stand on his own; he was therefore both the Liang army's help and its burden, and he was finally defeated at the river bridge, taken and killed at Linying. The most important figure on the Wei side was Erzhu Rong, the real master of Jinyang: he could strip the garrisons of the northern frontier of their troops and march them south within months, and he could break an enemy's defence on the Yellow River by crossing at night on rafts. Emperor Xiaozhuang Yuan Ziyou, for his part, went from emperor to pawn in his hands in this war, falling back to Zhangzi and then fleeing to Bingzhou. Among the local commanders, Qiu Daqian held Suiyang with nine forts and lost three of them in a single day, and was forced to surrender; Yuan Huiye was taken prisoner at Kaocheng; at Xingyang Yang Yu and his colleagues held out stubbornly while Lu An threw down his arms in the open field; and in the storming of Xingyang two braves, Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianjian of Yixing, were the first onto the wall. On the way back, people of Yuzhou, Cheng Daoyong and his companions, secretly escorted Chen Qingzhi out through Ruyin to Jiankang and so saved him from capture.
kits: 先要說清楚：卡面這具羅馬弩砲（Scorpio，前50年）並沒有出現在529年的睢陽戰場上。它是羅馬共和末期從希臘化世界承襲的扭力弩砲，一發一具箭，靠扭力簧片把拉力存住，箭在導軌上平射出去，主要用於攻守城；前50年前後，羅馬人正用它拆希臘城邦的城牆。把它放進這場戰役的裝備表，是因為它是重砲攻城這一技術譜系的源頭，而這條譜系早已東傳：經帕提亞、薩珊波斯與中亞一路傳入中國，在中國典籍裡以弩車、床子弩、砲車一類大型機弩的形式出現，儲能方式、導軌與釋放機構同屬一個技術家族。529年的睢陽攻防，恰恰是攻城技術與攻城補給的雙重考場。梁軍在梁國、睢陽一線所倚仗的攻城器械，包括臨城的弩機、雲梯與撞車一類攻具；守城一方則靠九座互援的城壘、弓弩居高射擊與牆頭反擊，把大批兵力壓在一片水網與城垣之間。考城四面環水，陳慶之在水面築壘進攻，用的仍是圍城打援、逼近決戰的老辦法；滎陽則因敵援不斷而至一度無法強攻，改為乘夜攀城，據《梁書》記載，一次擊鼓，梁軍便全部登上城牆。騎兵是梁軍真正的骨幹：護送北還時出動七千人，滎陽城下背城而戰的三千人是精騎，魏方與之對抗的是爾朱吐沒兒五千胡騎與魯安九千夏州步騎；陳慶之自己不擅騎射，他倚仗的是馬匹的機動力與士氣。運輸靠牛車，魏軍考城被攻破後被繳獲的租車就有七千八百輛，那是北魏的賦稅車隊，說明這場戰爭裡最有價值的東西是糧食與輜重；梁軍攻下滎陽後收繳的牛馬穀帛不可勝計，事實上是靠繳獲維持了遠征。糧秣與馬匹的極限，最後還是壓垮了這支深入之師。
kitsEn: First, one thing has to be said clearly: the Roman scorpio on the card, dated 50 BC, did not itself appear on the battlefield of Suiyang in 529. It was a torsion artillery piece inherited by the late Roman republic from the Hellenistic world, firing one bolt at a time, holding its pull in twisted skeins of sinew and sending the bolt flat along a track; it was used mainly in siege and defence, and around 50 BC the Romans were using exactly this to break the walls of the Greek city states. It belongs in the equipment table of this war because it is the source of the technological line of heavy artillery for siege, and that line had long since travelled east: through Parthia, Sasanian Persia and Central Asia into China, where it appears in Chinese sources as the large mechanical crossbow in the forms of the crossbow cart, the bed crossbow and the bolt-thrower, with the same family of principles for storing energy, for the track and for the release mechanism. The fighting at Suiyang in 529 was therefore an examination both of siege technique and of the supply of siege warfare. The siege equipment on which the Liang army relied along the line of Liangguo and Suiyang included crossbow engines mounted against the wall, scaling ladders and battering rams of the kind that are classed as assault devices; the defenders on the other side relied on nine mutually supporting forts, on bows and crossbows shooting from the height, and on counterattacks from the parapet, holding a large body of men between a net of water and the city wall. Kaocheng was ringed by water on four sides, and Chen Qingzhi attacked it by building a platform out over the water, using the old method of besieging and beating up the relieving force to force a decision; Xingyang, where enemy relief kept arriving and could not be stormed, was taken in the end by scaling the wall at night, and the Liang Shu records that at a single beat of the drum the whole army was on the wall. Cavalry was the true backbone of the Liang force: seven thousand men marched out to escort Yuan Hong north, and the three thousand who fought with their backs to the city at Xingyang were picked cavalry, opposed by the five thousand Hu horsemen of Erzhu Tumo'er and the nine thousand foot and horse of the Xia prefecture under Lu An. Chen Qingzhi himself was no horseman and no archer; what he relied on was the mobility of horses and the morale of his men. Transport was by ox cart, and when the Wei force at Kaocheng was broken the Liang took seven thousand eight hundred tax carts, which were the tax wagons of Northern Wei, showing that the most valuable things in this war were grain and baggage. The oxen, horses, grain and silk seized after Xingyang fell, in quantities that could not be counted, were in fact what kept the expedition alive. The limits of grain and horses were what finally crushed this army that had gone so far in.
tactics: 陳慶之的戰法可以用四個字概括：輕兵疾進，不與敵爭一城一池之地。528年十月他只帶七千人出發，一路上不攻城池、不留守軍，只求盡快抵達睢陽這個南北樞紐；529年四月攻入滎城與梁國之後，敵將丘大千分築九城拒守，陳慶之不逐一攻取，而是一日之內連破三城，擊潰守軍的信心，逼丘大千出降——這是把攻城當速戰來打，用一天的時間差製造崩潰。攻考城則用另一手：該城四面環水、守備嚴固，他在水面築壘，硬造出接近的通路，再以攻具近迫。滎陽是全戰最險的一關，初次強攻不下，魏援軍又至，他解鞍餵馬，向將士說明敵我眾寡懸殊、騎兵不可與敵於平原爭衡，唯有攻其城壘；隨後一次擊鼓，全軍登城，東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣率先上城，滎陽遂下。緊接著他以三千騎背城而戰，擊潰援軍，魯安陣前投降，元天穆、爾朱吐沒兒單騎而走，隨後乘勝取虎牢，魏方西線崩解。撤退時的處置同樣說明他的水準：爾朱榮挾重兵南來，他不與其爭鋒，收攏步騎數千結陣東撤，試圖以整陣自保；追兵跟到嵩高之下，適逢河水上漲，方陣被水勢衝散，隊伍才告瓦解。這套打法並非憑空而來：527年渦陽之戰中，他先以二百騎奔擊魏軍前鋒破其銳氣，後以銜枚夜出陷其四壘，再排列俘虜首級鼓噪而攻，一舉瓦解餘下九城；526年壽春，他攻拔李長鈞所築兩城逼降李憲；525年前後送豫章王蕭綜鎮徐州之時，他進逼魏軍新築的壘而魏軍一鼓即潰，亂軍之中他斬關夜退、全軍而還。佯敗、夜襲、排列俘虜以亂敵心、斬關夜退，都是梁書本傳明載的具體手法，也是這支遠征隊伍能連續攻克三十二座城池的技術底子。
tacticsEn: Chen Qingzhi's method can be summed up in four words: light troops in haste, not contesting a single town or pool of water with the enemy. In October 528 he set out with seven thousand men, and on the way took no walled towns, left no garrison behind, and sought only to reach Suiyang, the hinge between north and south, as fast as possible. After entering Liangguo in April 529 the enemy general Qiu Daqian distributed seventy thousand men among nine forts to hold him off, and Chen Qingzhi did not take them one at a time: he broke three of them inside a single day, broke the confidence of the defenders and forced Qiu Daqian to surrender. This is siege treated as a fast battle, with the compression of time itself producing the collapse. Against Kaocheng he used a different device: the city was ringed by water on four sides and strongly held, so he built a platform over the water, forcing a means of approach, and then brought the assault engines close. Xingyang was the most dangerous passage of the whole war. The first storming failed, and the Wei relief arrived, so he unbuckled his saddle and fed the horses, and told his men that the enemy were far more numerous, that cavalry should not be matched with the enemy in the open plain, and that the only course was to break into their fortified camp; then, at a single beat of the drum, the whole army was on the wall, Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianjian of Yixing first of all, and Xingyang fell. Immediately after that he fought with three thousand cavalry with their backs to the city and broke the relieving army; Lu An threw down his arms, Yuan Tianmu and Erzhu Tumo'er fled single-handed, and Hulao was taken on the momentum of the victory, collapsing the Wei line in the west. His handling of the withdrawal is a fair measure of his quality: when Erzhu Rong came south with a great army he did not try to match it, but drew his foot and horse, some thousands in number, into a formed column and marched east, trying to keep the whole body of men together; the pursuers followed him to below Mount Song, where the river came up and the column was scattered by the flood, and only then did the force dissolve. None of this was improvisation. At Woyang in 527 he first struck the Wei vanguard with two hundred horsemen to break its edge, then went out at night with the men holding their breaths to take four of the enemy forts by surprise, and finally paraded the severed heads of his prisoners and charged with noise to break the remaining nine. At Shouchun in 526 he took the two cities built by Li Changjun and forced Li Xian to surrender. Around 525, while escorting the Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong to take up his command at Xu, he closed on a newly raised Wei fort and the Wei broke at a single beat; in the general confusion he cut through the passes and withdrew by night with the whole army intact. Feigned retreat, night assault, the parrying of captured heads to shake the enemy's nerve, and cutting through the passes to withdraw by night are all specific methods recorded in the Liang Shu, and they are the technical foundation on which this expedition took thirty-two cities in succession.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是《梁書》《南史》與《資治通鑑》卷一百五十三所記的作戰數字：出師時陳慶之率兵七千人護送元顥北還；睢陽方面，丘大千眾七萬、分築九城，陳慶之一日攻下三城而克之；考城方面，魏征東將軍元暉業率羽林庶子二萬屯守，陳慶之築壘水上攻之，俘元暉業，獲租車七千八百輛；滎陽方面，魏左僕射楊昱、西河王元悰、撫軍將軍元顯恭率御仗、羽林、宗子、庶子眾七萬據守，援軍方面元天穆率眾三十萬、爾朱吐沒兒領胡騎五千、魯安領夏州步騎九千、爾朱世隆與王羆領騎一萬據虎牢，而梁軍出戰者為三千騎；戰果方面，《梁書》概括為自發銍縣至洛陽十四個月、平三十二城、四十七戰；洛陽城頭童謠作名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍；爾朱榮南下時眾號百萬，元顥據洛陽六十五日，陳慶之守北中郎城三日十一戰，終因河橋失守而潰，收攏步騎數千結陣東撤，追至嵩高因河水上漲而士卒死散殆盡。第二類是後世文人的概括，如十四個月、四十七戰、三十二城這組數字，是本傳追述全程的總數，與逐日記載難以逐一對應。第三類須打折扣：魏軍的三十萬、百萬與爾朱榮的眾號百萬顯係誇大，實際投入睢陽、滎陽一線的守軍當以數萬計；梁軍初起只有七千人，縱有沿途歸附之眾，總量仍在數萬之內。地理上，考城在睢陽東北約五十公里，滎陽在洛陽之東，虎牢在滎陽西北汜水鎮，洛陽之東有河橋，北中郎城則在今孟州附近；這些距離可由今地推定，但史書本身只記行程而未記里數。陳慶之本人484年生、539年卒，年五十六，卒後贈散騎常侍、左衞將軍、鼓吹一部，義興郡發五百丁會喪，這幾項屬於可核的年表數字。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first class is what the Liang Shu, the Nan Shi and the Zizhi Tongjian in volume 153 record of the fighting. On the march out Chen Qingzhi had seven thousand men to escort Yuan Hong north. On the Suiyang side, Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men distributed among nine forts, and Chen Qingzhi took three of them in a single day and carried the rest. At Kaocheng, Yuan Huiye, general who conquers the east, held twenty thousand of the Feathered Guard and the sons of noble families; Chen Qingzhi built a platform over the water and attacked, took Yuan Huiye prisoner, and captured seven thousand eight hundred tax carts. At Xingyang, Yang Yu the left director of the ministries, Yuan Jiong prince of Xiyuan and Yuan Xiangong general of pacification held some seventy thousand of the imperial guard, the Feathered Guard, the sons of the imperial clan and the sons of noble families; among the relieving force Yuan Tianmu came with three hundred thousand, Erzhu Tumo'er with five thousand Hu horsemen, Lu An with nine thousand foot and horse of the Xia prefecture, and Erzhu Shilong with Wang Ji held ten thousand cavalry at Hulao, while the Liang force that fought was three thousand cavalry. On the results, the Liang Shu sums it up as fourteen months from the departure at Zhi county to Luoyang, thirty-two cities taken and forty-seven battles fought. The rhyme sung at Luoyang ran: no great general or commander holds the pass, a thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses shun the white robe. When Erzhu Rong came south his host was numbered at a million; Yuan Hong held Luoyang sixty-five days; Chen Qingzhi fought behind the Northern Zhong city for three days and eleven battles and was broken at last by the loss of the river bridge, gathering some thousands of foot and horse into a column and marching east, pursued to Mount Song where the rising river left his men dead and scattered. The second class is the summary figures of later writers, such as the set of fourteen months, forty-seven battles and thirty-two cities, which are totals of the whole course as the biography retells it and cannot be matched item by item against the day-by-day record. The third class must be discounted. Wei's three hundred thousand, its million, and Erzhu Rong's host numbered at a million are plainly exaggerated; the troops actually committed on the Suiyang and Xingyang lines must have numbered in the tens of thousands, while the Liang army began with seven thousand and, allowing for all who joined on the way, stayed in the tens of thousands. Geographically, Kaocheng lies about fifty kilometres north-east of Suiyang, Xingyang lies east of Luoyang, Hulao lies north-west of Xingyang at Sishui, there was a river bridge east of Luoyang, and the Northern Zhong city was near present Mengzhou; these distances can be worked out from the modern map, but the histories record only the march and no count of li. As for Chen Qingzhi himself, he was born in 484 and died in 539 at the age of fifty-six, was posthumously granted the office of Scarlet Feathered Regular Attendant and Commander of the Left Guard with one set of musical honour, and the commandery of Yixing sent five hundred men to his funeral; these are checkable entries in the chronology.
cause: 打起來的原因，遠在睢陽城牆之外。第一層是北魏的內亂：528年十月孝明帝死，孝莊帝元子攸即位，實際掌權的是晉陽大將爾朱榮，他以邊鎮強兵威脅京師，殺戮宗室，朝廷威信盡失。北海王元顥正是看到這一點才出奔南梁，而梁武帝立刻接住這面旗子——擁立一個魏王的旗號，等於給北伐提供了合法性。第二層是北魏同時在別處失血：529年幽州流民邢杲起義，河北震動，北魏不得不在北面投入重兵；魏廷又想趁南方梁軍北進的同時在淮北用兵，兩面受敵。第三層是梁廷的算盤：梁與魏在鍾離、壽陽一線拉鋸多年，淮北是南北爭奪的關鍵地帶，梁武帝希望藉一次成功的北進取得政治聲望與實際控制；他對北方亂局也有相當準確的判斷，知道魏廷此刻調不動兵。第四層是陳慶之本人：多年散財招士，等的就是一個大局面，而梁武帝的信任給了他執行的空間。技術層面上，這支軍隊的設計從頭到尾圍繞一個字：快。七千輕兵不帶攻城重器、不守新取城池，目標是趁魏軍分散、逐次擊破其外圍據點，把戰果變成補給，而不是把城池變成包袱。魏方真正的失誤，是在睢陽的九城連失三座、在考城全軍被俘、在滎陽被夜襲攻破之後，仍把主力分散在虎牢、大梁、梁、宋四處，既無法集中，也沒有明確的統一指揮者，等於把陳慶之最擅長的速戰逐一送到他面前。
causeEn: The reasons for the war lay far beyond the walls of Suiyang. The first layer is the disorder inside Northern Wei: in October 528 Emperor Xiaoming died, Emperor Xiaozhuang Yuan Ziyou was installed, and the power was actually held by Erzhu Rong, the commander at Jinyang, who used the frontier garrisons to overawe the capital, killed members of the imperial clan and left the court without credit. Prince Yuan Hong of Beihai was precisely the man who, seeing this, fled to the south to the Liang, and Liang Wudi took up the banner at once, for setting up a King of Wei gave the expedition its legitimacy. The second layer is that Northern Wei was bleeding in another quarter at the same time: in 529 the rising of Xing Gao among the refugees of Youzhou shook Hebei and forced the north to commit heavy troops, while the Wei court at the same moment wanted to operate in the Huai north as the Liang armies moved north, and was thus pressed from two sides. The third is the Liang court's own calculation. Liang and Wei had been grinding against each other along the Zhongli and Shouchun line for years, and the Huai north was the key ground contested between south and north; Liang Wudi hoped for a successful advance to gain political prestige and actual control, and he read the disorder in the north with fair accuracy, knowing that the Wei court could not move its troops at that moment. The fourth is Chen Qingzhi himself: after years of scattering his money to gather soldiers and officers, what he was waiting for was a large situation, and the trust of Liang Wudi gave him the room to act on it. At the technical level the design of this army turned on a single idea: speed. Seven thousand light troops carried no heavy siege equipment and garrisoned no town they took; the object was to move in while the Wei were divided, break their outer strongholds one at a time, and turn victories into supply rather than turn towns into burdens. The real mistake of the Wei side was that after losing three of the nine forts at Suiyang, after the whole force at Kaocheng was captured, and after Xingyang was taken by a night assault, they still scattered their main strength between Hulao, Daliang, Liang and Song, unable either to concentrate or to find a single commander, and so they handed Chen Qingzhi, one at a time, exactly the kind of fast battle he was at his best in.
impact: 短期的影響大得驚人：梁軍十四個月平三十二城、四十七戰，攻入大梁、滎陽、虎牢，一度把洛陽握在手中，北魏孝莊帝退保長子、奔往並州，京師百僚備法駕迎元顥入洛陽宮、進而改元大赦；陳慶之麾下悉著白袍，名師大將莫自牢、千兵萬馬避白袍的童謠在洛陽城內流傳，白袍自此成為中國軍事史上一個鮮明意象，而陳慶之在梁書本傳中的位置，也因這一役被抬到與南朝諸名將並列的高度。長期影響則是反面的：這場北伐把梁的元氣與陳慶之的銳氣一起消耗在一次失敗裡，也讓北魏看清南朝並非無隙可尋；但真正決定歷史走向的不是陳慶之，而是爾朱榮。爾朱榮挾重兵掃平北魏內部的反對勢力，次年製造河陰之變、殺孝莊帝，北方從此在爾朱氏的鐵腕下重組，繼而爆發六鎮起義，孝武帝西遷長安，北魏裂為東魏、西魏；梁的北伐失敗，實際上只是這條崩解曲線上的一個小插曲，卻已經耗掉了南朝最重要的一次北進機會。對陳慶之個人而言，這一役是他一生的頂點也是轉折：從建康歸來後，他仍平定了僧強、蔡伯龍的北徐州之亂，圍懸瓠，破婁起、是雲寶、孫騰、侯進、堯雄、司馬恭諸軍，開田六千頃，罷義陽鎮兵、停水陸轉運，使江湖諸州得到休息；大同二年東魏侯景率眾七萬寇楚州，他又在黎漿擊破侯景，雪中收其輜重而還。他卒於大同五年十月，年五十六，贈散騎常侍、左衞將軍。後世對他的推崇幾乎全集中在這一役上，毛澤東讀《南史·陳慶之傳》曾批注再讀此傳，為之神往，可見這段北伐在二十世紀的中國讀者心中同樣是一個不肯熄滅的火種。
impactEn: The short-term effect was startling: the Liang army took thirty-two cities and fought forty-seven battles in fourteen months, entered Daliang, Xingyang and Hulao, and for a time held Luoyang in its hand; the Wei Emperor Xiaozhuang fell back to Zhangzi and fled to Bingzhou, and the ministers of the capital came out with the imperial procession to welcome Yuan Hong into the Luoyang palace, where he changed the era and issued a general pardon. Chen Qingzhi's men all wore white, and the rhyme sung in Luoyang, no great general or commander holds the pass, a thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses shun the white robe, went round the city; the white robe became from that day a striking image in Chinese military history, and Chen Qingzhi's place in the Liang Shu biography was raised to the level of the other famous commanders of the southern court. The long-term effect, however, is the reverse. This expedition consumed the strength of the Liang and the edge of Chen Qingzhi alike in a single failure, and it showed the north that the southern court was not without openings. Yet what decided the course of history was not Chen Qingzhi but Erzhu Rong. Erzhu Rong used his great army to sweep away the opposition inside Northern Wei, and the next year manufactured the disaster on the Yellow River and killed Emperor Xiaozhuang; the north was reorganised under the iron hand of the Erzhu clan, the rising of the six garrisons followed, Emperor Xiaowu moved west to Chang'an, and Northern Wei split into Eastern and Western Wei. The failure of the Liang expedition was in truth only a small episode on that curve of disintegration, but it had already spent the most important northern opportunity of the southern court. For Chen Qingzhi himself the campaign was the summit of his life and the turning of it as well. After returning to Jiankang he went on to put down the rising of Seng Qiang and Cai Bolong in the northern Xu prefecture, to invest Xuanhu, to break the armies of Lou Qi, Shi Yunbao, Sun Teng, Hou Jin, Yao Xiong and Sima Gong, to open six thousand qing of fields, to disband the garrison at Yiyang and stop the river and road transport so that the provinces around the lakes might rest; and in the second year of the Datong era, when the Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing with seventy thousand men against Chuzhou, he broke Hou Jing at Lijiang and took his baggage away in the snow. He died in the tenth month of the fifth year of the Datong era at the age of fifty-six, and was posthumously granted the office of Scarlet Feathered Regular Attendant and Commander of the Left Guard. Almost all the later admiration for him is concentrated in this one campaign: Mao Zedong, reading the biography of Chen Qingzhi in the Nan Shi, wrote in the margin that to read it again fills him with longing, which shows that this northern expedition remained for twentieth-century Chinese readers too a fire that would not go out.
result: 結果分兩截。戰術上，梁軍是完勝到驚人的程度：529年四月一日之內連下睢陽三城，逼降丘大千；破考城，俘元暉業，殲羽林二萬，繳獲租車七千八百輛；兵鋒直指大梁，魏軍望風而降；滎陽一度攻不下，但趁援軍抵達、佈署未就，乘夜擊鼓登城，東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣先登頭陣，城破之後三千騎背城而戰，擊潰援軍，魯安陣前投降，元天穆、爾朱吐沒兒單騎而走；虎牢隨之易手；梁軍進洛陽，陳慶之受封衛將軍、徐州刺史、武都公，進侍中、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，增邑萬戶。戰略上則是徹底的失敗：529年閏六月，爾朱榮自晉陽率大軍南下，與元顥隔黃河對峙，派木筏夜渡擊破河防，元顥僅以數百騎走至臨潁被擒殺，洛陽復歸北魏；陳慶之收攏步騎數千結陣東撤，仍被追至嵩高，適逢河水上漲，隊伍在追擊中死散殆盡，他自己化裝成僧人西行，由豫州人程道雍等暗送出境，經汝陰回到建康。梁廷沒有因敗績加罪，反而記功除右衛將軍、封永興縣侯，邑一千五百戶。一句總結：這是一場以七千輕兵起步、靠速度與士氣贏下所有城池、卻終究被補給與援軍拖垮的深入戰役；陳慶之證明了一支小軍隊可以在十四個月裡摧毀一個帝國的外圍，卻沒有能證明小軍隊可以佔領一個帝國。睢陽城下那些連下三城的工事，後來都成了史書裡白袍二字的註腳；而真正決定北魏命運的那支軍隊，既不在陳慶之的白袍裡，也不在元顥的宮殿裡，它在爾朱榮身後。
resultEn: The outcome has two halves. Tactically the Liang army won to a startling degree. In April 529 it took three of the forts at Suiyang within a single day and forced Qiu Daqian to surrender; it broke Kaocheng, took Yuan Huiye prisoner, destroyed twenty thousand of the Feathered Guard and captured seven thousand eight hundred tax carts; its point drove straight at Daliang and the Wei forces surrendered as it came; Xingyang could not at first be stormed, but as the relieving force arrived and was not yet deployed, the drums beat at night and the wall was climbed, Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianjian of Yixing first of all, and after the city fell three thousand cavalry fought with their backs to it and broke the relief, Lu An threw down his arms and Yuan Tianmu and Erzhu Tumo'er fled single-handed; Hulao changed hands soon after; the Liang entered Luoyang, and Chen Qingzhi was made General of the Guard, Inspector of Xu and Duke of Wudu, and then given the offices of Attendant of the Household, General of the Chariot and Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Left Light, with his fief increased by ten thousand households. Strategically it was an outright defeat. In the intercalary sixth month of 529 Erzhu Rong marched south from Jinyang with a great army and faced Yuan Hong across the Yellow River, sent rafts over at night and broke the river defence, and Yuan Hong fled with a few hundred horsemen to Linying, where he was taken and killed; Luoyang returned to Northern Wei. Chen Qingzhi gathered some thousands of foot and horse into a column and marched east, was pursued as far as Mount Song, and there the rising river left his men dead and scattered almost to the last; he himself disguised himself as a monk and travelled west, and the people of Yuzhou, Cheng Daoyong and his fellows, smuggled him out of the country and sent him by way of Ruyin back to Jiankang. The Liang court did not punish him for the failure; on the contrary it recorded his merit, made him Commander of the Right Guard and Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of fifteen hundred households. To sum it up in one sentence: this was a deep penetration that began with seven thousand light troops, won every city it touched on speed and morale, and was still dragged down in the end by supply and by the relieving armies. Chen Qingzhi proved that a small army can destroy the outer ring of an empire in fourteen months; he did not prove that a small army can occupy one. The works that fell three in a day below Suiyang afterwards became little more than a gloss on the two characters for the white robe in the histories; and the army that truly decided the fate of Northern Wei was neither in Chen Qingzhi's white robes nor in Yuan Hong's palace. It was behind Erzhu Rong.
